title: Tool Federation and Lazy Output PRD (WIP)
content:
Context:
This doc records an exploratory PRD for a latency-first Hosted API feature set: tool federation + lazy/progressive output + SDK ergonomics to support mid-stream tool resolution and incremental structured outputs. Goal is minimal coordination cost for clients, robust graceful degradation when federated tools are slow/unavailable, and clear dev ergonomics for SDKs (web + mobile + server).

Problem statement:
- Customers embedding realtime assistants frequently need multiple heterogeneous tool providers (search, code-exec, DB lookup, booking APIs). Right now hosted-api SDKs expect a single tool graph and synchronous tool resolution or full client-managed orchestration. That forces either: (a) blocking > high latency, or (b) complex client logic and retry semantics.
- Streaming partial responses are valuable but current partial output semantics make it hard to attach structured tool results consistently (race conditions, duplicate tool calls, unclear commit boundaries).

User personas:
- Product engineer building a chat assistant that calls search + knowledge graph + calendar. Needs low response latency for initial suggestions and later enriched answers when slow tools return.
- Platform integrator building an endpoint for multiple internal tool backends where availability varies. Wants predictable SLA and fallback behaviors.
- Mobile app dev who needs SDK ergonomics for low-bandwidth, intermittent networks and resume semantics.

High-level proposal:
1) Tool federation: hosted-api supports a declared list of tool endpoints (federated tool registry). Each tool has metadata: compat-version, priority, estimated-latency, required/optional flag, idempotency-hint, and structured-output schema reference. The runtime will (by policy) fan-out calls in parallel or sequence per request profile.
2) Lazy/progressive output frames: extend streaming frames with three logical layers: partial-text frame, tool-placeholder frame, and committed-tool-result frame. Each frame is typed and includes an action-id that ties placeholders to eventual results. Clients can choose render modes: optimistic-fill (show placeholder + speculative text), hold-until-commit, or hybrid.
3) SDK ergonomics: surface a small set of client APIs to manage placeholders, tool metadata, and replay. Provide default adapters for web (JS), mobile (Swift/Kotlin), and server (Go/Python) that implement backpressure and resumable sessions. SDK should give easy hooks: onPlaceholder, onToolProgress, onToolResult, onFrameCommit.

Key behaviors and invariants:
- Exactly-once intent for tool invocations: the server must avoid double-execution for tools marked idempotent=false; use action-id + de-duplication window. For cross-service federation where uniqueness can't be guaranteed, fall back to best-effort with explicit result-warning frames.
- Response latency SLOs: initial partial-text should be emitted within 120ms median for short prompts on dedicated tiers; tool-result commits can stream in later when available.
- Graceful degradation: optional tools that fail/time out result in a lightweight warning frame and continue the stream; mandatory tools time out per policy and cause either: (a) fallback result (from a cached/approx model), or (b) abort with structured error frame depending on route config.

Example stream sequence (simplified):
- frame(0): partial-text "Here are some ideas..."
- frame(1): tool-placeholder action-id=abcd type=search schema=v1
- frame(2): partial-text "Top result looks like: " (optimistic)
- frame(3): tool-progress action-id=abcd progress=50%
- frame(4): tool-result action-id=abcd {structured search JSON}
- frame(5): commit action-id=abcd (indicates tool result is final and associated tokens are stable)

Config surface for route/model:
- federation_policy: {parallelism=auto|serial|highest-priority-first} (SDK sees friendly enums, server stores flags)
- tool_timeout_ms: per-tool override
- placeholder_mode: optimistic|hold|hybrid
- max_pending_tools_per_session: integer
- de_dup_window_ms: 300000

SDK design notes / ergonomics:
- Keep public API tiny: onStreamFrame(frame) where frame.type in {text, placeholder, progress, toolResult, commit, error}. Provide helpers to reconstruct the transcript and correlate action-ids.
- Local caching layer for tool results with TTL and storage-agnostic implementation (in-memory for mobile; LRU for server).
- Backpressure: when a device cannot keep up with incoming frames, SDK should advertise window sizes; server will apply client_window token to throttle progressive fidelity.
- Offline resume: session tokens allow resuming from last-acked commit. Placeholders persist client-side until commit or expiration.

Open questions / risks:
- Security / auth model for federated tools: tools can be customer-owned (on-prem endpoints) or Redwood-managed connectors. Need clear auth handshake + token scoping.
- Cost accounting: if server fans out to many federated tools in parallel, billing/chargeback becomes nontrivial. Explore attribution model (per-tool charge + base token cost) or aggregated bucket.
- Consistency semantics with tool retries: how to present duplicate or conflicting results to the model and client? Propose `conflict` frames with provenance metadata.
- Latency pathology: optimistic UI may show wrong/unsafe results if tool result contradicts speculative text. Need a strategy for automatic redaction or user-visible correction.

Milestones (proposed):
- Sep–Oct: API sketch + federation schema + frame types (internal).
- Nov–Dec: server runtime prototype (federation router + placeholder frames) + JS SDK prototype.
- Jan–Feb: integrator beta with 3rd-party tool connectors (search, SQL, calendar); mobile SDK adapters.
- Mar: limited beta customers + perf/regression tests + cost model analysis.

Playbook recommendations for initial launch:
- Default placeholder_mode=optimistic for dev tiers, hold for enterprise by default.
- Expose opt-in telemetry: placeholder-mismatch-rate (fraction of optimistic text that needed correction), tool-latency distribution per tool, and duplication_count.
- Provide a debugging UI in Console: session inspector that can filter frames by action-id and visualize tool timelines.

Notes to self / todo:
- Draft wireframes for Console session inspector (timeline + frame search).
- Call infra to validate de-dup approach with KV cache TTL patterns.
- Legal: check PII leaking risk when sending placeholders or partial tokens to federated tools.

References / inspiration:
- existing partial-response contract docs (see linked artifacts)
- patterns from distributed tracing for correlating action-ids across services

This is intentionally exploratory; expecting tradeoffs and follow-up design sessions. Comments welcome inline.
